OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. It is normalized before being stored and
            returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and internal runs of whitespace
            collapsed to a single space, the value is upper-cased and common abbreviations are
            expanded as whole tokens (ST -> STREET, RD -> ROAD, AVE -> AVENUE). So
            '  12  main  st ' is stored and returned as '12 MAIN STREET'. An address that is
            blank after normalization is rejected with 400. Household duplicate detection and
            the shared household id both compare addresses in this normalized form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized into E.164 form: a
            leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces,
            dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must contain 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. So '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'. The pattern
            tolerates an optional leading '+' plus digits and separators (spaces, brackets,
            dashes); numbers that cannot form valid E.164 are rejected with 400.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it must be a
            syntactically valid email address. The value is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 3
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional on
            create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner already shares the
            same last name and address (compared case-insensitively, with runs of whitespace
            collapsed). When omitted or false, such a duplicate is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

            id:

              description: The ID of the pet owner.

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for owner registration dates in the Spring Boot app. All changes are in `ClinicServiceImpl.java`:

**1. Effective date adjustment (`saveOwner`)** — For new owners, the *effective* registration date is computed as the supplied date if present, otherwise the server's current date (`LocalDate.now()`). That effective date is then rolled forward onto a business day via a new `toBusinessDay(...)` helper and stored as `registrationDate`:

```java
LocalDate effectiveDate = owner.getRegistrationDate() != null
    ? owner.getRegistrationDate()
    : LocalDate.now();
owner.setRegistrationDate(toBusinessDay(effectiveDate));
```

This covers both paths and changes the previous behaviour, where a supplied weekend date was stored as-is.

**2. `toBusinessDay` helper** — Saturday rolls forward two days and Sunday one day, both landing on the next Monday; weekdays pass through unchanged.

**3. Derived values use the adjusted date** — Because `registrationDate` is adjusted *before* `ownerRepository.save` and before the DTO mapping, the membership number's year segment (`OwnerMapper.formatMembershipNumber`, which reads `registrationDate.getYear()`) automatically uses the adjusted date.

**4. Daily create-limit counts per adjusted business day (`isDailyRegistrationAtCapacity`)** — It now buckets against `toBusinessDay(LocalDate.now())` instead of raw today, matching the adjusted dates that owners are stored with (otherwise, on a weekend, the stored Monday dates would never match a raw-Saturday count).

Note: the spec I was given only covers weekend rolling (→ next Monday). The test base happens to also expose a holiday-aware `toBusinessDay` helper, but the active test (`coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay`) only asserts the result is never Saturday/Sunday, and the spec says nothing about holidays — so I kept the implementation to exactly what was specified. The model's `@PrePersist` default remains as a harmless fallback (it's no longer reached on the create path since the service always sets the date).

**3. Derived values use the adjusted date** — Because `registrationDate` is adjusted *before* `ownerRepository.save` and before the DTO mapping, the membership number's year segment (`OwnerMapper.formatMembershipNumber`, which reads `registrationDate.getYear()`) automatically uses the adjusted date.
